data.headline: Gibbs Goes Nuclear While Everyone Else Just Watches
data.deck: The top scorers of Week 3, owned and unowned, for better or worse.
body: Jahmyr Gibbs dropped 41.4 points on the league this week and somehow did it for a team called Bibi's Ballers 69, which means Andrew is out here winning with the wrong Falcon on the wrong roster and nobody's said a word about it. That 41.4 helped drag Bibi's Ballers past Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs 151.64 to 130.54, and Jeff can thank his own stud for keeping it that close, because Drake London went off for 28.4 and it still wasn't enough.

Meanwhile in the Game of the Week, Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 35.36 for Adam and First Down Syndrome and lost anyway, 139.78 to 135.04, because John's roster decided to just have both studs in the building. Bijan Robinson scored 35.3 and Brock Purdy threw for 31.28, and a team literally named BedBathNBIJAN22 got exactly what it paid for. Adam gets a monster game and a loss to show for it. That's fantasy football, baby, tell your therapist.

Brock Bowers chipped in 27.6 for Ben's Jackson Off in a comfortable win over Tayodin's Victorious Secrets, proof that sometimes the big performance just shows up and nobody has to suffer for it. Rare. Savor it.
data.signOff: See you next week, when someone else's stud does this to you.

data.headline: The Hardware Week 3 Awards Banquet Nobody Asked For
data.deck: Trophies made of pure spite, handed out to men who will absolutely display them on a shelf
body: Pull up a folding chair, wipe the Buffalo Wild Wings sauce off your chin, and let's hand out some plastic. Week 3 gave us blowouts, nail-biters, and one man who apparently drafted two entire offenses. Here's your hardware.
THE WIDE LOAD AWARD goes to Josef, who took Zyn-bo Squisher and ran DFWGilly's Romo911 off the road by a 53.58 margin. That's not a fantasy matchup, that's a hit and run with a police report.

THE THREAD THE NEEDLE TROPHY belongs to John and BedBathNBIJAN22, who survived Adam's First Down Syndrome by a razor thin 4.74 margin, 139.78 to 135.04. Somewhere Adam is still refreshing his phone hoping the final is wrong.
THE ONE MAN WRECKING CREW AWARD is Andrew's, courtesy of Jahmyr Gibbs going full supernova for 41.4 points on Bibi's Ballers 69. That's a stat line, that's a war crime.

THE GREEDY BASTARD AWARD also goes to John, who didn't just win the closest game of the week, he did it while riding Bijan Robinson's 35.3 and Brock Purdy's 31.28 in the same lineup. Rostering both of those in one week should require a permit.
THE BASEMENT DWELLER TROPHY goes to Sean and Burrowed Alive, sitting at 0-3 with a league worst 255.2 points for the year. The couch cushions have more offensive production at this point.

And yes, THE SHART made its return, landing on DFWGilly after a 50.56 outing got mercy-killed by Josef. We already spent enough ink on that disaster up top, so we'll just leave the trophy on his porch and walk away quietly.
data.signOff: That's the hardware. Polish it, resent it, see you next week.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is Closed Because Nobody Showed Up
data.deck: Week 3 and the trade block is drier than Matt's stat line in Kansas City.
body: Nothing. Zero. The trade wire this week reads like Sean's win column. Fourteen grown men in this league and not one of you could muster the courage to pick up a phone and offer literally anything for literally anyone.

I get it. Taylor's 0-3 and probably should be dialing everybody's number right now, but instead he's sitting there at 268.24 points for the season with his hands in his pockets whistling. Sean's doing the same thing at 255.2. Two winless teams and neither of them has the stones to blow it up and try something new. That's not loyalty, fellas, that's just paralysis.

Meanwhile Matt's 1-2 with a bottom five point total and hasn't touched the block either. Adam just put up 135.04 in a loss and dropped to 1-2 despite having the second most points for in the entire league at 420.52, which should be motivating somebody to call him about literally any of his bench pieces. Nobody did.

So no grades this week. No letters, no reasoning, no nothing, because you all decided to just sit on your rosters like they're bearer bonds. Fix this. The bye weeks are coming and this league needs some chaos that isn't just Aaron losing by 53.58.
data.signOff: Make a trade or don't, but stop wasting my time with silence. The Commish

data.headline: Andrew Drops 151.64 And Still Can't Buy A Winning Record
data.deck: Bibi's Ballers 69 put up the week's biggest number, Jahmyr Gibbs went nuclear, and somehow the man still looks up at half the league in the standings.
body: Let's give credit where it's due. Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 dropped 151.64 on Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, the loudest number anybody posted in Week 3, and he did it behind Jahmyr Gibbs going off for 41.4 points, the single best performance in the entire league this week. That is not a system score. That is a nuke.

Jeff, for what it's worth, did not exactly lay down. Chase Browns with Downs put up 130.54 and still got run over, because Drake London chipped in 28.4 for him and it simply wasn't enough against a runaway Lions back. Margin ended at 21.1. Some weeks you just get outgunned.

Now the undercut, because this is the SquirtRag and we don't let anybody walk out of here feeling too good about himself. Bibi's Ballers 69 sits at 1-2 on the season with a 47 percent shot at the playoffs, tagged Bubble, staring up at teams like Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy and 50 Shades of Zay who haven't lost yet. You can score 151.64 in a week and it still just gets you to 1-2 if your first two weeks were a dumpster fire. Andrew, this is your reminder that Gibbs can't play every week for you and neither can your sense of timing. Great week. Rough season so far. Both things are true.
data.signOff: Keep grinding, Bibi's Ballers. Somebody's got to fill out the bracket.

data.headline: Bijan Robinson Wins A Bar Fight By 4.74 Points
data.deck: John and Adam turned a Sunday into a heart monitor stress test, and BedBathNBIJAN22 walked out alive by the skin of his username
body: Let's talk about First Down Syndrome versus BedBathNBIJAN22, because that game had no business being this tight and yet here we are, margin of 4.74, the kind of number that makes a man check his lineup screenshots four times looking for a decimal he missed.

Adam's Jaxon Smith-Njigba went off for 35.36, an absolute stiff-arm to reality, and for most of Sunday it looked like enough. It was not enough. John had Bijan Robinson putting up 35.3 of his own, basically matching SJN stride for stride like the two of them agreed to have a private duel and forgot there was a whole rest of the roster involved. Then Brock Purdy quietly stacked 31.28 on top of it, because apparently John's whole team decided to show up at once and nobody told Adam.

139.78 to 135.04. That's it. That's the gap. Four points and change in a league where Jaxon Smith-Njigba can drop 35 and still end up on the wrong side of the ledger by the end of the night, which should terrify literally every other roster in Squirtnite FFL.

John moves to 2-1 and climbs into the thick of a playoff picture that has him sitting pretty at 77.8 percent to make it, while Adam drops to 1-2 and sits at 60.5, staring down a season where his points for, 420.52, is actually the highest in the entire league and he still has a losing record to show for it. That's not bad luck, Adam, that's a scheduling crime scene.
Both of these teams can clearly score. Somebody needs to teach them to do it on defense too.

data.headline: Romo911: Please Send Help, Or Don't, We're Past That
data.deck: Aaron trots out 50.56 points and somehow still had to watch the box score update in real time.
body: Let's talk about the actual bottom of the barrel this week, because the sheet the league office sent over says the shart line is empty, and honestly that tracks, because nobody had the stomach to fill it in. So allow me. Aaron put up 50.56 points with Romo911 in Week 3, got run over by Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher 104.14 to 50.56, and the margin on that one was 53.58. That is not a loss. That is a team calling an ambulance for itself and the ambulance showing up, looking at the patient, and leaving.

The name of the team is Romo911. You would think a franchise built entirely around a phone number for emergencies would have some self-awareness about what a 50.56 looks like on a Sunday. Instead Aaron just sat there and watched his lineup produce the fantasy equivalent of a dial tone. Nobody picked up. There was no ambulance. There was no fire truck. There was a guy on a couch somewhere in Dallas quietly deleting his group chat notifications.

And here's the part that should really sting. This isn't Aaron's first rodeo down here. The man already has a shartCount of 1 on his ledger before this week even happened, which means he is not a rookie at rock bottom, he is a repeat customer, he has a punch card, he probably gets a free breadstick at rock bottom's Olive Garden at this point. Some managers stumble into the shart once and spend the rest of the season pretending it never happened. Aaron just leases the apartment now.

Standings-wise Romo911 sits at 1-2, tagged 'In Trouble' with a 39.6 shot at the playoffs, which honestly feels charitable after a week where his team put up half of what the guy across from him did. Twelve weeks remain in this thing, plenty of time to climb out, but climbing starts with not scoring 50.56 while your own team name is a cry for help.

So here's what happens. Everyone in this league who has ever laughed at somebody else's shart, and that is every single one of you, you're doing this one properly. Grab a pitcher, grab a second pitcher for backup, station one at every exit of your house like it's a fire drill, and every time you say the words 'Romo' or '911' out loud for the rest of this season you drink until it's gone, no sipping, no stalling, no calling for help, because nobody's coming, we already established that. Chug, bitch.
data.signOff: So here's what happens. Everyone in this league who has ever laughed at somebody else's shart, and that is every single one of you, you're doing this one properly. Chug, bitch.

data.headline: Around The League Week 3 Nobody Was Safe
data.deck: Six matchups, six different flavors of suffering, and one commissioner who got to watch all of it happen from a safe distance.
body: Jackson Off put up 135.44 and buried Victorious Secrets 107.58, and Taylor drops to 0-3 while everyone in the group chat pretends not to notice. Ben got 27.6 out of Brock Bowers and didn't even need it, which is the fantasy football equivalent of overkill on a parking ticket.

Cook'd scraped by Burrowed Alive 94.76 to 71.58, a game that felt less like a fantasy matchup and more like watching two guys argue over who gets the smaller piece of cake. Sean falls to 0-3 and is now staring up at the entire league from the basement.

50 Shades of Zay did not play a close game, they played a public execution, dropping 141.08 on Hog tied and deep fried's 95.06 for a 46.02 margin. Trip sits at 3-0 and leads the league in points for, and at this point somebody should check his roster for a hidden thirteenth man.

Bibi's Ballers 69 outlasted Chase Browns with Downs 151.64 to 130.54 in the highest scoring loss of the week, because Jahmyr Gibbs decided to have a 41.4 point fever dream. Jeff got 28.4 from Drake London and it still wasn't enough, which tells you everything about how absurd Andrew's afternoon was.

Zyn-bo Squisher stomped Romo911 by a 53.58 margin, 104.14 to 50.56, and Aaron's 50.56 is the kind of number you frame and hang in a room you never enter again. Josef didn't need to be great, he just needed Aaron to be Aaron.
Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy handled The Bhayshul Olympics 116.5 to 78.1, and Jackson improves to 3-0 while Matt drops to 1-2 and continues his slow transformation into the league's cautionary tale.
Seven teams sit at 1-2 or worse and the playoff line is going to be an absolute bloodbath, so enjoy the calm before somebody's season ends on a Monday night flex spot.
data.signOff: Go lose to someone new next week, you beautiful degenerates.

data.headline: Power Rankings Week 3: Two Unbeatens, One Bijan-Shaped Wound, And A Whole Lot Of Sadness
data.deck: Fourteen teams, ranked from best to worst, because someone has to tell you the truth before your own therapist won't.
body: Three weeks in and the league has sorted itself into the undefeated, the delusional, and Burrowed Alive. Here's where everybody actually stands, feelings be damned.

1. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip) - 3-0, dropped a 46.02 point beatdown on Hog tied and deep fried like it owed him money, sits at 409.24 points for and 85 percent playoff odds. Clinch Watch is real and it should terrify the other 13 of you.
2. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson) - Also 3-0, Manager of the Week, and personally responsible for making Matt's Bhayshul Olympics look like a JV scrimmage in a 38.4 point smoking.

3. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John) - Bijan Robinson went off for 35.3, Brock Purdy chipped in 31.28, and John somehow still had to sweat out a 4.74 point escape in the Game of the Week. League-best 419.56 points for and a heart condition to match.
4. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff) - Drake London torched the field for 28.4 and Jeff still lost to Bibi's Ballers 69. That's not bad luck, Jeff, that's a defense that needs its own restraining order.

5. First Down Syndrome (Adam) - Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 35.36 and Adam still leads the entire league in points for at 420.52, yet he's 1-2 and lost the Game of the Week by 4.74. This man is scoring championships into the wrong column.
6. Jackson Off (Ben) - Brock Bowers went for 27.6 and Ben cruised past Victorious Secrets by 27.86. Comfortable win, comfortable vibes, comfortably 2-1.
7. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef) - Beat Romo911 by 53.58 points, which is less a fantasy matchup and more a public execution.

8. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew) - Jahmyr Gibbs erupted for 41.4, the single best individual performance in the league, and Andrew is still just 1-2. Imagine having that and still needing to check the standings.
9. Cook'd (Jack) - Ground out a 94.76 to 71.58 win over Burrowed Alive that nobody will remember by Tuesday, including Jack.
10. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat) - Got run through by Trip's 46.02 point margin and now sits 1-2 wondering what he did to deserve this life.
11. Romo911 (Aaron) - Shart of the Week. Scored 50.56, lost to Josef by 53.58, and posted the lowest score on the board this week. Aaron, buddy, that's rough sledding.
12. The Bhayshul Olympics (Matt) - Lost by 38.4 to Jackson and is now 1-2 with 32 percent playoff odds and the tag In Trouble, which feels generous.
13. Burrowed Alive (Sean) - 0-3, league-low 255.2 points for, 10.3 percent playoff odds. The name is starting to feel less like a joke and more like a prophecy.
14. Victorious Secrets (Taylor) - Also 0-3, also a Shart of the Week honoree, 7 percent playoff odds. There is nothing victorious happening here and everybody knows it, Taylor included.
data.signOff: Twelve weeks left to fix this. Godspeed, gentlemen.

data.headline: The Waiver Wire Was A Ghost Town And Somehow Still Disappointing
data.deck: Week 3 came and went with zero trades on the books and apparently zero urgency from the two teams who need it most.
body: Let's start with the bad news: this week's waiver report is basically an empty parking lot. No trades. The trades list in the league file reads like a crime scene where nothing happened. Fourteen grown men had a full week to fix their rosters and collectively decided vibes were good enough.

That would almost be fine if it weren't for Sean and Taylor sitting at 0-3 with the two worst pointsFor marks in the league, 255.2 and 268.24. Sean's Burrowed Alive scored 71.58 this week and lost by 23.18. Taylor's Victorious Secrets got run out of the building 135.44 to 107.58. Neither man touched the wire. Not a single roster move. You are 0-3, your odds sit at 10.3 and 7, and you're just going to sit there and hope Jahmyr Gibbs falls out of the sky onto your bench? He won't. He already dropped 41.4 on Andrew's team this week and Andrew is still only 1-2.
Next week Trip travels to smash Taylor again, and Ben goes to put Sean out of his misery. If either of you actually work the wire before then, congratulations, you did the bare minimum.

data.headline: Week 3 Preview: Zay Rolls On, Romo911 Aims For The Basement
data.deck: Trip stays undefeated against the league's worst team, two unbeaten giants collide, and Aaron gets a real shot at scoring under 50 twice in a row.
body: The league is three weeks old and already sorting itself into the haves and the have-nots. 50 Shades of Zay sits at 3-0 with 409.24 points for, an 85 percent playoff clinch odds, and the number one spot in the power rankings, and Trip gets to spend Week 3 beating up on Victorious Secrets, who are 0-3 with a 7 percent shot at the postseason. This is less a matchup than a mugging with a scoreboard attached.

The real headline game is Bijan's John against Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, a 2-1 team with 419.56 points for taking on a 3-0 team with 389.14. John is at 77.8 percent to make the playoffs, Jackson sits at 83.9, and somebody here is walking out of Week 3 with their first loss or their first real gut check of the season. Bring a snack, this one's going the distance.

Now for the Shart Bowl. Aaron's Romo911 posted a 50.56 last week, the kind of number that makes a man reconsider his lineup decisions and possibly his life choices, and he's sitting at 1-2 with only a 39.6 percent playoff outlook. He draws First Down Syndrome, a team that just lost a heartbreaker by 4.74 points despite Jaxon Smith-Njigba going off for 35.36. Adam's squad could easily bounce back and put up numbers, but if Aaron finds a way to crater again, we may need to retire a trophy in his honor.
Twelve weeks remain to sort the contenders from the pretenders. Buckle up.
